Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Tempered dark chocolate: Tempering warms and cools chocolate so cocoa butter crystals line up, giving a glossy finish and a crisp snap.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Blue steak: 'Blue' comes from the French 'bleu': barely seared outside with an almost raw inside.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Rare steak: Searing doesn't seal in juices, that's a myth; it builds flavour through browning.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Medium-rare steak: The favoured doneness of many chefs, and the meat rises a few degrees while resting.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Medium steak: The pink fades as the pigment myoglobin changes at around 60 °C.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Medium-well steak: Only slightly pink, as the heat has tightened proteins and squeezed out more moisture.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Well-done steak: This is the USDA temperature for ground beef, because grinding mixes surface bacteria into the middle.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Safely cooked chicken: The USDA threshold that kills salmonella instantly, though lower temperatures also work if held long enough.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Baked sandwich loaf: The crumb is done when the centre reaches about 88 to 93 °C, when starch has fully set.
Internal temperatures: chocolate to pull.Pull-apart tender pork: Around this temperature collagen melts into gelatin, which is why pork shoulder turns tender and shreddable.

The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Library of Congress founded: Founded with about 740 books when Congress moved to Washington, it is now among the largest collections ever assembled.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.UK-Ireland union takes effect: The union created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, and the Union Jack gained St Patrick's saltire.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Peace of Amiens: A brief truce between Britain and Napoleonic France, it collapsed in about a year.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Louisiana Purchase: The US paid France about $15 million and roughly doubled in size.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Napoleon crowned emperor: He took the crown from the Pope's hands and placed it on his own head at Notre-Dame.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Battle of Trafalgar: Nelson died at the hour of victory, after signalling 'England expects that every man will do his duty'.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Holy Roman Empire dissolved: Francis II abdicated the throne of an empire whose roots reached back to Charlemagne's coronation in 800 or Otto I's in 962.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Britain bans the slave trade: This banned the trade, but slavery itself in British colonies lasted until 1833.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Peninsular War begins: Spanish fighters gave English the word 'guerrilla', meaning 'little war'.
The first decade of the 1800s, one per y.Lincoln and Darwin born: Both great men were born on 12 February 1809, the same day, an ocean apart.

When these odd bans began.Football (London): Edward II outlawed the rowdy street game in London in 1314, in what is the earliest known law against football.
When these odd bans began.Kissing (England): Henry VI is said to have banned kissing to slow the spread of plague, though historians doubt this was ever really enforced.
When these odd bans began.Coffee (Mecca): Governor Khair Beg banned it in Mecca, fearing it encouraged dissent, but the sultan in Cairo overturned the ban.
When these odd bans began.Tobacco (Ottoman Empire): Sultan Murad IV reportedly punished smoking with execution, though the ban faded after his death in 1640.
When these odd bans began.Christmas (England): Puritan Parliament banned Christmas feasting as unholy; riots broke out, and the holiday returned in 1660 under Charles II.
When these odd bans began.Beer (Iceland): Iceland's alcohol ban eased in 1935, but strong beer stayed illegal until 1 March 1989, now celebrated every year as Beer Day.
When these odd bans began.Alcohol (USA): Prohibition lasted 13 years and fuelled bootleggers and speakeasies; the 21st Amendment repealed it in 1933.
When these odd bans began.Pinball (New York City): Mayor La Guardia smashed confiscated machines with a sledgehammer, calling them gambling devices; the ban stood until 1976.
When these odd bans began.Late-night dancing (Japan): Japan's 1948 law regulating dance venues was only loosened in 2015, after a campaign by clubbers and a few well-known legal cases.
When these odd bans began.Chewing gum (Singapore): Gum sales were banned over litter and vandalism; since 2004 only therapeutic gum is allowed, sold through pharmacies.

Old and odd units of length.Fermi: The fermi is named for physicist Enrico Fermi, and it's handy for nuclear physics, since a proton is about one femtometre across.
Old and odd units of length.Ångström: The Ångström is named for Swedish physicist Anders Ångström, and it is still used for atom sizes and light wavelengths.
Old and odd units of length.Mil (thou): The mil, or thou, is a thousandth of an inch, and machinists and electronics makers still use it for tiny tolerances.
Old and odd units of length.Barleycorn: The barleycorn was an actual barley grain, and three of them made an inch in medieval England.
Old and odd units of length.Hand (horse height): Horse height is measured in hands, and the unit descends from the width of a human hand, with fractions in inches.
Old and odd units of length.Cubit: The cubit was the distance from elbow to fingertip, and ancient Egypt's royal cubit was standardized on a stone rod.
Old and odd units of length.Fathom: A fathom is six feet, roughly the span of outstretched arms, and sailors used it for measuring depth with a lead line.
Old and odd units of length.Furlong: A furlong is eight to a mile and it comes from a furrow's length, and horse races in Britain are still measured in them.
Old and odd units of length.League: A league was roughly the distance a person could walk in an hour, and Jules Verne's 20,000 Leagues is about depth, not distance.
Old and odd units of length.Parsec: The parsec is used for stellar distances, and its name comes from parallax of one arcsecond, not a unit of time as Han Solo suggested.

The first of their kind online.Trojan Room coffee pot cam: The Trojan Room coffee pot cam at Cambridge let researchers check if the coffee was ready, and it became the world's first webcam.
The first of their kind online.First photo on the web: The first photo on the web showed Les Horribles Cernettes, a band of CERN staff, and it was uploaded by Tim Berners-Lee's colleague.
The first of their kind online.First secure online purchase: The first secure online purchase is said to be a Sting CD, sold using encryption in 1994.
The first of their kind online.First eBay sale: The first eBay sale was a broken laser pointer, and the founder was shocked that someone wanted to buy it.
The first of their kind online.First Google Doodle: The first Google Doodle was a stick figure behind the logo, and it was a note that the founders were away at Burning Man.
The first of their kind online.First Wikipedia edit: Wikipedia began in 2001, and its first edits were small tests, and it has since grown into the largest encyclopedia.
The first of their kind online.Me at the zoo (YouTube): Me at the zoo is a short video of co-founder Jawed Karim at San Diego zoo, and he talks about elephants' long trunks.
The first of their kind online.First tweet: The first tweet, by Jack Dorsey, read just setting up my twttr, and it was sent in March 2006.
The first of their kind online.First Bitcoin transaction: The first Bitcoin transaction sent coins from Satoshi Nakamoto to Hal Finney, and it was part of a test.
The first of their kind online.First Instagram photo: The first Instagram photo was a dog's paw and a taco stand in Mexico, and posted by co-founder Kevin Systrom.

Cats from tiniest to biggest.Rusty-spotted cat: Found in India and Sri Lanka, it is among the world's smallest wild cats, about half the size of a domestic cat.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Sand cat: Fur-padded paws let it walk on hot desert sand, and it can survive without drinking, getting moisture from its prey.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.House cat: Domestic cats have lived alongside people for roughly 10,000 years, and they purr at a frequency of about 25 to 150 hertz.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Ocelot: Its coat pattern is unique to each animal, and it hunts at night across forests from Texas to Argentina.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Eurasian lynx: Ear tufts and a stubby tail mark the biggest lynx, which hunts deer in cold northern forests.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Snow leopard: Its long thick tail helps balance on cliffs and wraps around its face like a scarf in freezing Himalayan winds.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Leopard (male): Leopards haul prey as heavy as themselves up trees to keep it from lions and hyenas.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Jaguar (male): Jaguars kill by biting through the skull, and their bite is the strongest relative to size among the big cats.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Lion (male): Lions are the only cats living in prides, and a male's mane darkens and thickens with age and testosterone.
Cats from tiniest to biggest.Siberian tiger (male): Also called the Amur tiger, it is the largest living cat, adapted to the snowy forests of Russia's Far East.

Retailers, by founding year.Harrods: Harrods, in London's Knightsbridge, began as a grocery and tea shop; it later built a famous escalator, once a novelty that offered brandy to nervous riders.
Retailers, by founding year.Macy's: Macy's was founded by Rowland Hussey Macy, and its star logo is said to come from a tattoo he got as a young whaling sailor.
Retailers, by founding year.Woolworth: F.W. Woolworth pioneered the five-and-dime store with fixed prices, which let shoppers browse freely and pick up items themselves.
Retailers, by founding year.Marks & Spencer: Marks & Spencer started as a penny bazaar in Leeds, with the slogan 'Don't ask the price, it's a penny'.
Retailers, by founding year.Selfridges: Harry Gordon Selfridge, an American, opened his Oxford Street department store with the motto 'The customer is always right', famed for window displays.
Retailers, by founding year.Tesco: Tesco was founded by Jack Cohen, whose name combined with the initials of a tea supplier's name, T.E. Stockwell, gives the name.
Retailers, by founding year.IKEA: IKEA's name comes from founder Ingvar Kamprad's initials plus the first letters of his farm Elmtaryd and village Agunnaryd.
Retailers, by founding year.Walmart: Walmart began with Sam Walton's discount store in Arkansas and is now the world's largest company by revenue.
Retailers, by founding year.The Home Depot: The Home Depot was founded in Atlanta by Bernie Marcus and Arthur Blank, who had both been fired from another home-improvement chain.
Retailers, by founding year.Etsy: Etsy started as a marketplace for handmade goods and craft supplies, and its name was reportedly inspired by hearing the Italian 'etsi'.

When these treaties and pacts were agree.Egyptian-Hittite peace treaty: Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III agreed to this treaty after the Battle of Kadesh, and a copy is displayed at the United Nations.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Peace of Nicias: The Peace of Nicias paused the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta, though it collapsed within a few years.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Treaty of Apamea: The Treaty of Apamea ended the war between Rome and the Seleucid king Antiochus III, and made Rome the major power in the east.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Treaty of Verdun: The Treaty of Verdun divided Charlemagne's empire among his three grandsons and set the stage for what would become France and Germany.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Treaty of Wedmore: The Treaty of Wedmore saw the Viking leader Guthrum accept Christianity, after Alfred the Great defeated him, and led to the Danelaw.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Concordat of Worms: The Concordat of Worms settled the Investiture Controversy, and decided how popes and emperors would share power over bishops.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Golden Bull of Charles IV: The Golden Bull of 1356 set out how the Holy Roman Emperor would be chosen by seven electors, and it governed Germany for centuries.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Treaty of Windsor: The Treaty of Windsor between England and Portugal is the oldest continuous diplomatic alliance in the world.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Peace of Lodi: The Peace of Lodi ended wars between Milan and Venice, and helped bring a few decades of stability in Italian city-states.
When these treaties and pacts were agree.Treaty of Tordesillas: The Treaty of Tordesillas split the New World between Spain and Portugal along a line drawn in the Atlantic, which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.

Units of time.Nanosecond: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, and light travels only about 30 centimeters in that time.
Units of time.Microsecond: A microsecond is a millionth of a second, and the typical camera flash lasts about a thousand microseconds.
Units of time.Millisecond: A millisecond is a thousandth of a second, and a honeybee beats its wings about five times in one.
Units of time.Second: The second was once defined as a fraction of a day and is now defined by the vibrations of a cesium atom.
Units of time.Minute: The minute comes from the Latin for 'small part', and its division into 60 comes from ancient Babylonian counting.
Units of time.Hour: An hour has 3,600 seconds, and the 24-hour day is thought to come from ancient Egypt.
Units of time.Day: A day is slowly lengthening because the tides pull on the Earth, by about 2 milliseconds per century.
Units of time.Week: The seven-day week has no astronomical basis, and probably came from Babylonian or Jewish tradition.
Units of time.Fortnight: Fortnight comes from the Old English for 'fourteen nights', and it is still used in British English.
Units of time.Lunar month: A lunar month is the time from one new moon to the next, about 29.5 days, which is why calendars like the Islamic one follow the moon.

Rodents from tiny to giant.African pygmy mouse: One of the world's smallest rodents, adults are just a few centimetres long, and it lives in sub-Saharan Africa.
Rodents from tiny to giant.House mouse: Mice travelled the world alongside humans, and their genome holds about as many genes as ours, roughly 20,000.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Mongolian gerbil: Gerbils drum their hind feet as an alarm, and pet gerbils all descend from a few dozen caught in Mongolia in 1935.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Brown rat: Despite also being called the Norway rat, it came from Asia and spread globally by ship.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Chinchilla: Chinchillas have up to 60 hairs per follicle, and they bathe in dust because water mats their fur.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Muskrat: It builds dome lodges of reeds and mud in marshes and can stay underwater for about 15 minutes.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Groundhog: Also called a woodchuck, it truly hibernates, which is why Punxsutawney Phil's Groundhog Day forecast takes place in February.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Patagonian mara: These long-legged rodents live in monogamous pairs, and mothers leave their young in communal creches.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Beaver: Its orange teeth contain iron and never stop growing; it is the largest rodent in Europe and North America.
Rodents from tiny to giant.Capybara: The largest rodent in the world is semi-aquatic, can sleep in water with just its nose out, and often has birds perched on it.

Battery capacities.Hearing aid cell: It is a zinc-air battery that switches on when you peel the sticker and let air in.
Battery capacities.LR44 button cell: This small alkaline cell powers calculators and toys.
Battery capacities.CR2032 coin cell: The code means 20 mm wide and 3.2 mm thick, and it often powers key fobs and watches.
Battery capacities.Rectangular 9-volt: Inside a typical alkaline 9-volt are six small cells stacked together.
Battery capacities.AAA alkaline: It is just 44 mm long and 10 mm wide, and typically powers remotes and small devices.
Battery capacities.AA alkaline: The AA is the most common household battery, the size used in remotes and toys.
Battery capacities.Smartphone battery: Lithium-ion cells slowly lose capacity with use, and after roughly 500 full cycles a phone battery noticeably weakens.
Battery capacities.C alkaline: Size determines capacity and not voltage, as a C has the same 1.5 volts as an AAA.
Battery capacities.D alkaline: It has the same voltage as a AA but a much larger capacity, lasting far longer in flashlights.
Battery capacities.Car battery: The lead-acid battery, invented by Gaston Planté in 1859, is the oldest rechargeable type.

How much does a newborn weigh?.Red kangaroo joey: Born about the size of a jellybean, blind and hairless, it crawls unaided into its mother's pouch.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Giant panda cub: A newborn panda is roughly 1/900 of its mother's weight, pink, blind and nearly hairless.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Polar bear cub: Cubs are born in a snow den in winter, blind and tiny, and nurse on rich milk until spring.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Lion cub: Cubs are born with faint spots that fade as they grow, and their eyes open after about a week.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Human baby: Unlike most mammals, human newborns are helpless and born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse later.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Bottlenose dolphin calf: Calves are usually born tail-first, and the mother nudges the newborn to the surface for its first breath.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Hippo calf: Hippos often give birth in water, and calves can nurse underwater by closing their ears and nostrils.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Giraffe calf: Born standing up, a calf drops over a meter to the ground at birth and can stand within an hour.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Elephant calf: Calves take months to master their trunks and sometimes trip over them while the herd guards them.
How much does a newborn weigh?.Blue whale calf: A newborn is around 7 meters long and gains roughly 90 kg a day on its mother's fat-rich milk.

How big they look in our sky.Uranus: Barely visible to the naked eye, it was discovered in 1781 by William Herschel.
How big they look in our sky.Mars (at its biggest): Even at its best the red planet is tiny; its color comes from iron oxide, rust, in its soil.
How big they look in our sky.Jupiter (at its biggest): Galileo spotted its four biggest moons in 1610, and good binoculars can show them today.
How big they look in our sky.Venus (at its biggest): It looks largest when it is a thin crescent near Earth, so biggest doesn't mean brightest.
How big they look in our sky.Crab Nebula: This supernova remnant was recorded by Chinese astronomers in 1054, and it has a pulsar spinning about 30 times a second.
How big they look in our sky.Full Moon: A pea held at arm's length covers it, and you can see it in all its phases.
How big they look in our sky.Orion Nebula: Visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy patch in Orion's sword, it's a stellar nursery about 1,300 light-years away.
How big they look in our sky.The Pleiades: Japan's Subaru logo depicts this star cluster, which is called Subaru in Japanese.
How big they look in our sky.Andromeda Galaxy: The nearest big galaxy, about 2.5 million light-years away, it appears several Moons wide on a dark night.
How big they look in our sky.The Big Dipper: An asterism within Ursa Major, its end stars point the way to Polaris.

Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Basil Rathbone: He starred in 14 films from 1939, with Nigel Bruce as Watson. His version put the character in a deerstalker, though that was first drawn by Sidney Paget.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Peter Cushing: Better known as Grand Moff Tarkin, he starred for Hammer Films in The Hound of the Baskervilles and later played the detective on British TV.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Nicol Williamson: He played Holmes in the 1976 film The Seven-Per-Cent Solution, written by Nicholas Meyer, in which the detective is treated for cocaine use by Sigmund Freud.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Christopher Plummer: He played Holmes in Murder by Decree (1979), opposite James Mason's Watson, hunting Jack the Ripper. He is best known as Captain von Trapp.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Jeremy Brett: He played the detective in Granada's TV series, which began in 1984 and ran for a decade, and he is often considered the closest to the books.
Guy Ritchie's 2009 film cast him as a fighting, action-oriented Holmes, with Jude Law as Watson, and spawned a sequel in 2011.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Benedict Cumberbatch: The 2010 BBC series Sherlock updated the detective to the present day, with a smartphone and a blog, and made him a global star.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Jonny Lee Miller: CBS's Elementary, from 2012, put the detective in modern-day New York, with Lucy Liu as a female Watson.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Ian McKellen: He played an aged Holmes in the 2015 film Mr. Holmes, based on a novel about the detective in retirement, keeping bees.
Actors' first time playing Sherlock Holm.Henry Cavill: He played Sherlock in the 2020 Netflix film Enola Holmes, as the older brother of Millie Bobby Brown's title character, and he is Superman's actor too.

Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Granicus: Alexander's first major victory in Asia Minor in 334 BC, in which he nearly died when a blow cracked his helmet.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Gordium: Alexander is said to have sliced through a legendary knot here, which promised rule over Asia to whoever undid it.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Issus: Alexander defeated Darius III here in 333 BC, and the Persian king fled, leaving behind his family.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Memphis: Alexander was welcomed here as a pharaoh, and he founded the first Alexandria nearby.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Gaugamela: The decisive battle with Darius III took place on open plains in 331 BC, and Alexander won despite being outnumbered.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Babylon: Alexander entered this great city without a fight, and he died here in 323 BC, probably at about 32.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Susa: Alexander seized the Persian royal treasury here, and it held a vast hoard of silver and gold that funded his army.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Persepolis: The Persian ceremonial capital; Alexander's army burned its palace, perhaps as revenge for Xerxes' burning of Athens.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Samarkand: This Silk Road city is in modern Uzbekistan, and Alexander passed through it during his campaign in Central Asia.
Alexander's battles and cities, by dista.Hydaspes: Alexander's last great battle in 326 BC was against King Porus, and he later founded a city here for his horse Bucephalas.

Birth years of computing pioneers.Charles Babbage: He designed the Difference Engine and Analytical Engine, never finished in his life. London's Science Museum built a working Difference Engine in 1991.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Ada Lovelace: Lord Byron's daughter wrote what is often called the first computer program, for Babbage's Analytical Engine, and foresaw machines making music.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Herman Hollerith: His punched-card tabulators sped up the 1890 US census, and the company he founded later became part of IBM.
Birth years of computing pioneers.John von Neumann: His stored-program design, in which instructions and data share the same memory, still underlies most computers today.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Alan Turing: He helped break Germany's Enigma at Bletchley Park, and also proposed the test of machine intelligence that now carries his name.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Claude Shannon: His 1948 paper founded information theory and brought the word 'bit' into wide use. He also built a mechanical mouse that solved mazes.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Bill Gates: He co-founded Microsoft in 1975, after leaving Harvard, and became the world's richest person.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Linus Torvalds: The Finnish student began the Linux kernel in 1991 as a hobby, and later also created the Git version-control system.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Mark Zuckerberg: He launched Facebook from a Harvard dorm room in 2004, and it grew to billions of users.
Birth years of computing pioneers.Vitalik Buterin: At 19 he proposed Ethereum, a blockchain that can run programs called smart contracts, and he is its best-known co-founder.

How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Flea: Fleas can jump about 100 times their own length, thanks to a springy protein called resilin.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Honeybee: A honeybee beats its wings about 230 times a second, and that fast flutter is the buzz you hear as it passes.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.House mouse (body): Mice can squeeze through gaps barely wider than a pencil, because their ribs and skull are very flexible.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.House cat (body): Cats spend roughly two-thirds of their lives asleep, around 13 to 16 hours a day, in many short naps.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Emperor penguin (standing): Male emperor penguins incubate the egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter, fasting for about two months.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Komodo dragon: The largest living lizard, found on a few Indonesian islands, has venom glands in its lower jaw.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Great white shark: Great whites replace their teeth throughout life, with rows of spares behind the front ones, as they wear down.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Orca: Orcas are the largest dolphins, hunt in pods, and different pods have their own hunting techniques and calls.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Sperm whale: Sperm whales have the biggest brain of any animal, about 8 kg, and dive over a kilometer deep.
How long (or tall) is a typical adult?.Blue whale: The blue whale is the largest animal known ever, bigger than any dinosaur, and its low calls carry for many kilometers underwater.

Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Siderian: The name comes from Greek for iron, 'sideros', since banded iron formations were laid down as oxygen reacted with iron in the oceans.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Rhyacian: Its name comes from the Greek for a stream of lava, and the period saw intense volcanic activity.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Orosirian: The name means 'mountain range' in Greek, and it includes the huge Vredefort impact, about 2.02 billion years ago.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Statherian: Its name means 'stable', for continental crust that had become steady.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Calymmian: The name comes from Greek for 'covering', for sediments that blanketed continental platforms.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Ectasian: Its name means 'extension', reflecting the spreading of sediment covers across platforms.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Stenian: The name means 'narrow', after narrow belts of metamorphic rock formed as the Rodinia supercontinent assembled.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Tonian: Its name means 'stretch', for the thinning crust as the supercontinent Rodinia began to break up.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Cryogenian: This 'Snowball Earth' period had glaciers possibly reaching the equator; the name means 'cold birth'.
Hardcore geology: the Proterozoic period.Ediacaran: Named for the Ediacara Hills of Australia, it was the first new geological period named in over a century, with early soft-bodied animals.

When these Near Eastern powers arose.Sumerian city of Uruk: Uruk, in southern Mesopotamia, is often called the world's first city, and it's where cuneiform writing is thought to have begun.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Akkadian Empire: Sargon of Akkad united Mesopotamia's city-states and created one of history's first empires, and spoke Akkadian.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Third Dynasty of Ur: Ur-Nammu's dynasty revived Sumerian rule, and he is credited with the oldest known law code, which predates Hammurabi.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Hammurabi's Babylon: Hammurabi's famous law code was carved on a stone slab, now in the Louvre, and includes the 'eye for an eye' principle.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Hittite Old Kingdom: The Hittites of Anatolia were early masters of iron and chariots, and they fought Egypt at the Battle of Kadesh.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Middle Assyrian Empire: Assyria became a major power again in this era, with its capital at Assur, after centuries of decline.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Neo-Assyrian Empire: Assyria's army was the most feared of its day, with iron weapons and siege engines, and its capital Nineveh had a famous library.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Neo-Babylonian Empire: Led by Nebuchadnezzar II, this Babylon built the Ishtar Gate and, tradition says, the Hanging Gardens.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Achaemenid Persia: Founded by Cyrus the Great, it became the largest empire of its time, stretching from Egypt to India's edge.
When these Near Eastern powers arose.Seleucid Empire: Founded by one of Alexander's generals, Seleucus I, it ruled a huge area from Syria to Central Asia after Alexander's death.

When these famous figures were born.Hammurabi: The Babylonian king whose law code, carved on a black stone, is among the oldest in the world, and set fines by social class.
When these famous figures were born.Ramesses II: The pharaoh who ruled 66 years, built Abu Simbel and probably fathered over 100 children.
When these famous figures were born.Confucius: His sayings were gathered into the Analects, and his teachings shaped East Asian society for over two thousand years.
When these famous figures were born.Socrates: He wrote nothing himself; we know him through Plato and others, and he was sentenced to drink hemlock.
When these famous figures were born.Alexander the Great: Taught by Aristotle, he conquered the Persian empire by his early thirties, and founded cities named Alexandria.
When these famous figures were born.Julius Caesar: He became dictator of Rome and was stabbed on the Ides of March, and the month of July is named for him.
When these famous figures were born.Augustus: Rome's first emperor, born Octavian, inherited power as Caesar's heir, and the month of August is named after him.
When these famous figures were born.Charlemagne: Crowned emperor on Christmas Day in 800, he united much of Western Europe and sparked a revival of learning.
When these famous figures were born.Genghis Khan: Born Temujin, he united the Mongol tribes and built the largest contiguous land empire in history.
When these famous figures were born.Joan of Arc: A teenage peasant girl from Domremy who led French troops against the English, and was burned at the stake at 19.

Big science machines, by when they start.Lawrence's cyclotron: The first cyclotron was small enough to hold in your palm, about 4 inches across, yet earned Ernest Lawrence a Nobel Prize.
Big science machines, by when they start.Chicago Pile-1 reactor: Enrico Fermi's team built it beneath the stands of a University of Chicago stadium, in a former squash court, and achieved the first self-sustaining chain reaction.
Big science machines, by when they start.Lovell Telescope, Jodrell: Its 76 m dish tracked the rocket that launched Sputnik within weeks of opening, and it's now named after astronomer Bernard Lovell.
Big science machines, by when they start.Arecibo Observatory: The Puerto Rican radio dish spanning 305 m starred in a James Bond film, and it collapsed in 2020 after cable failures.
Big science machines, by when they start.Very Large Array: Twenty-seven radio dishes on rails across the New Mexico desert act as one giant telescope, and it featured in the film Contact.
Big science machines, by when they start.Tevatron: This Fermilab collider found the top quark in 1995 and closed in 2011, two years after the Large Hadron Collider took over at the energy frontier.
Big science machines, by when they start.CERN's LEP collider: This 27 km ring tunnel under Switzerland and France was later emptied to make room for the Large Hadron Collider.
Big science machines, by when they start.Super-Kamiokande: Sitting deep in a Japanese mine, a tank of about 50,000 tonnes of water caught neutrino oscillations, which led to the 2015 Nobel Prize.
Big science machines, by when they start.LIGO observations begin: These twin detectors in the US sense space ripples shorter than a proton's width, and first caught gravitational waves from colliding black holes in 2015.
Big science machines, by when they start.Large Hadron Collider: Its 27 km ring is cooled colder than outer space, and it helped confirm the Higgs boson in 2012.

Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Selfie: Oxford said use of this word rose by about 17,000% in a year, partly thanks to its spread on social media.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Vape: Chosen from a shortlist that included 'normcore' and 'bae', it reflected the rise of e-cigarettes.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.😂 (the emoji): This was the first time an emoji took the title; its official name is 'Face with Tears of Joy'.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Post-truth: Its use spiked around 2,000% in a year after Brexit and the US presidential election.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Youthquake: The word was coined in the 1960s by Vogue editor Diana Vreeland and revived after the 2017 UK general election.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Toxic: From Greek 'toxikon', meaning poison for arrows, it won after being one of the year's most-looked-up words.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Climate emergency: Oxford said use of the phrase rose by more than 10,000% in 2019, as 'climate crisis' also surged.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Goblin mode: It was the first Word of the Year decided by public vote, with over 300,000 people voting, about 93% for it.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Rizz: The slang is short for charisma; Tom Holland told a magazine he had 'no rizz whatsoever'.
Oxford Words of the Year, in order.Brain rot: Dating back to Thoreau's Walden in 1854, it surged in the 2020s to describe the effects of junk online content.

Countries of the Americas by population.Belize: Belize is the only country in Central America where English is the official language, and it has the world's second-largest barrier reef.
Countries of the Americas by population.Uruguay: Uruguay legalized same-sex marriage and cannabis early, and it held the first FIFA World Cup in 1930, which it won.
Countries of the Americas by population.Cuba: Cuba has been called an island of classic cars, and its health system trains many doctors who serve abroad.
Countries of the Americas by population.Chile: Chile is about 4,300 km long yet averages less than 200 km wide, and its Atacama is one of the driest places on Earth.
Countries of the Americas by population.Peru: Peru was home to the Inca Empire and gave the world potatoes, and has thousands of native potato varieties.
Countries of the Americas by population.Canada: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined, and most of its people live close to the US border.
Countries of the Americas by population.Colombia: Colombia is one of the most biodiverse countries and a top exporter of coffee and cut flowers.
Countries of the Americas by population.Mexico: Mexico has the largest Spanish-speaking population of any country, and it also recognizes dozens of indigenous languages.
Countries of the Americas by population.Brazil: Brazil is the largest nation in South America and the only one where Portuguese is the main language.
Countries of the Americas by population.United States: The United States is the most populous country in the Americas, with no official national language at the federal level.

The Ramayana, in story order.Rama breaks Shiva's bow: Sita's swayamvara asked suitors to lift and string Shiva's mighty bow; Rama snapped it in two, winning her hand.
The Ramayana, in story order.Exile to the forest: Because of a boon granted to Queen Kaikeyi, Rama was sent away for fourteen years, followed by Sita and Lakshmana.
The Ramayana, in story order.Surpanakha humiliated: Ravana's sister fell for Rama; when she was rejected, Lakshmana cut off her nose, setting the war in motion.
The Ramayana, in story order.The golden deer: The demon Maricha took the shape of a golden deer to lure Rama away from Sita.
The Ramayana, in story order.Sita abducted by Ravana: Ravana carried Sita off in a flying chariot, and the vulture Jatayu died trying to stop him.
The Ramayana, in story order.Rama meets Hanuman: The monkey devotee first appears disguised as a scholar, and so begins an alliance with the monkey king Sugriva.
The Ramayana, in story order.Vali is slain: Rama shot the monkey king from hiding, a controversial act, and placed Sugriva on the throne.
The Ramayana, in story order.Hanuman sets Lanka ablaze: Lanka's guards set his tail alight, and he used it to burn much of the golden city.
The Ramayana, in story order.Bridge built to Lanka: Monkey builders raised the bridge across the sea, said to be stones that floated when marked with Rama's name.
The Ramayana, in story order.Ravana is slain: The ten-headed king dies in battle, and Dussehra still celebrates it with burning effigies each autumn.

Odds of these chance events.Winning 6/49 lotto: The odds are about 1 in 14 million, so you're likelier to be struck by lightning in your lifetime.
Odds of these chance events.Dealt a royal flush: Roughly 1 in 650,000 five-card hands is a royal flush.
Odds of these chance events.Yahtzee on the first roll: Five of a kind on one roll is 1 in 1,296.
Odds of these chance events.Drawing the ace of spades: Any one specific card has the same 1 in 52 chance, and a well-shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order never seen before.
Odds of these chance events.Rolling double six: Snake eyes are exactly as likely as double six, at 1 in 36.
Odds of these chance events.Drawing an ace: Four aces among 52 cards give 4 in 52, or 1 in 13.
Odds of these chance events.Three heads in a row: Each flip is independent: three heads in a row is 1 in 8, but the next flip is still 50-50.
Odds of these chance events.Rolling a six: Dice have been found in digs around 5,000 years old, and yet the chance of a six has never changed.
Odds of these chance events.Two coins both heads: The chance of two heads is the product of two halves, one quarter.
Odds of these chance events.Coin lands heads: A real coin is not perfectly fair, since researchers have shown it lands on its starting side about 51 percent of the time.

Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Jason loses a sandal: Crossing a river, Jason carried an old woman, who was the goddess Hera in disguise, and he lost a sandal, fulfilling a prophecy.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.The Argo is built: Built with Athena's help, it included a talking beam from the sacred oak of Dodona.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.The women of Lemnos: The women had killed all the men, so Jason's crew stayed a while with their queen, Hypsipyle.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Hylas lost to the nymphs: Heracles' young companion was pulled underwater, and Heracles left the voyage to search for him.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Phineus and the Harpies: The blind seer was tormented by Harpies who stole his food, until two Argonauts chased them off.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.The Clashing Rocks: Jason released a dove to test the rocks, and the ship slipped through with just its stern ornament lost.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Yoking fire-breathing bulls: The bronze-hoofed bulls of King Aeëtes breathed fire, but Medea's ointment protected Jason.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Sowing the dragon's teeth: The teeth grew into armed warriors, and Jason threw a stone among them so they fought each other.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.The fleece is stolen: Medea put to sleep the dragon that guarded the golden ram's fleece, which once carried Phrixus.
Voyage of the Argonauts, in story order.Talos the bronze giant: A bronze giant guarded Crete, with a single vein sealed by a nail, and Medea tricked him to his death.

When these instruments first appeared.Hohle Fels bone flute: Carved from a vulture's wing bone in a German cave, it is among the oldest instruments ever found.
When these instruments first appeared.Lyres of Ur: Found in the Royal Cemetery at Ur, one has a gold bull's head, excavated by Leonard Woolley.
When these instruments first appeared.Hydraulis (water organ): Invented by Ctesibius in Alexandria, it used water pressure to keep air steady.
When these instruments first appeared.Harpsichord: It plucks strings, so it can't change loudness by touch, which helped inspire the piano.
When these instruments first appeared.Violin: Andrea Amati of Cremona set its form, and Stradivari later perfected it.
When these instruments first appeared.Piano: Bartolomeo Cristofori named it gravicembalo col piano e forte, soft and loud harpsichord.
When these instruments first appeared.Tuba: It was patented in Berlin by Wilhelm Wieprecht and Johann Moritz.
When these instruments first appeared.Ukulele: Portuguese immigrants brought its ancestor to Hawaii, and its name means 'jumping flea'.
When these instruments first appeared.Electric guitar (Frying Pan): This aluminum lap steel is considered the first commercial electric guitar.
When these instruments first appeared.Mellotron: Its eerie flute intro opens the Beatles' Strawberry Fields Forever.

A butterfly's life, step by step.Egg laid on a leaf: Females choose the right host plant by tasting it with their feet. The tiny egg is stuck to the leaf and may be laid singly or in clusters.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Caterpillar hatches: The young caterpillar is a hungry eating machine. It is built to grow, and may increase its weight by thousands of times.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Eats its own eggshell: Many caterpillars eat their eggshell first. It gives them nutrients and removes evidence that might attract predators.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Munches leaves and moults: A caterpillar outgrows its skin several times, shedding it in moults. Each stage between moults is called an instar.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Hangs upside down: Before pupating, the caterpillar spins a silk pad, and hangs from it in a J shape, or attaches a silk girdle. It stays still for hours.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Skin splits into a chrysalis: The final caterpillar skin splits to reveal the chrysalis beneath. Moths usually spin a silk cocoon, but butterflies mostly make a bare chrysalis.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Body rebuilds inside: Inside, most of the caterpillar's body breaks down into a kind of soup, and then rebuilds into a butterfly using special clusters of cells.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Butterfly breaks out: The adult emerges, and the empty chrysalis turns clear. It is damp, wrinkled and fragile at first, with soft folded wings.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Pumps up its crumpled wings: The butterfly pumps fluid into the veins of its wings to expand them, and then waits for them to dry and harden before flying.
A butterfly's life, step by step.Takes its first flight: Once its wings are dry, it flies off to feed on nectar and find a mate. Monarchs of the final generation migrate thousands of kilometres.

Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Aladdin meets Jasmine: Aladdin (1992) was the highest-grossing film in the United States that year, and Jasmine was Disney's first Arab-inspired princess.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Jafar tricks Aladdin: Jafar's name echoes Jafar al-Barmaki, a real vizier of Harun al-Rashid, who in history fell from power.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Inside the Cave of Wonders: The original tale was added to the Arabian Nights by Antoine Galland in the early 1700s and is set in China.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Genie appears from the lamp: Robin Williams recorded so much improvised material as the Genie that the filmmakers had hours of it to cut down.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Aladdin becomes Prince Ali: Prince Ali's parade is a showpiece number, and it highlights the film's theme of pretending to be someone else.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Magic carpet ride: A Whole New World won the Oscar for Best Original Song and a Grammy for Song of the Year.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Genie saves him from drowning: The Genie's rules for wishes are no killing, no love, and no raising the dead, so saving Aladdin's life is a wish.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Jafar steals the lamp: Iago the parrot is voiced by Gilbert Gottfried, and Abu the monkey is Aladdin's loyal thief.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Jafar wishes to be a genie: Wishing to be an all-powerful genie backfires, because genies are bound to the lamp.
Disney's Aladdin, in story order.Aladdin frees the Genie: Freeing the Genie ties to the film's theme of freedom, and the Genie's final wish is just to be free.
